summary.intent: Remove the insightsdb SQLite cache from the summary TUI and replace it with direct checkpoint store reads, reusing the data loading approach from the existing explain command. Also ensure all checkpoints are browsable in the TUI even without summaries, with on-demand generation.
summary.outcome: Deleted the entire insightsdb/ package, replaced insightsdb.SessionRow with a new SessionData struct, rewrote summary_cmd.go to load from checkpoint store via ListCommitted/ReadSessionContent, updated all tests, registered the summary command in root.go, removed the IsSummarizeEnabled guard, and committed the result.

repo: The `facets` package was imported by the WIP summary TUI code but never existed as a directory — the entire facets abstraction had to be removed rather than migrated.
`resolveMemoryLoopDefaultBranch` and `listReachableCheckpointIDs` were called in summary_cmd.go but never defined anywhere in the codebase — they were incomplete WIP stubs.
The summary command was defined in summary_cmd.go but never registered in cli/root.go; a test failure revealed this.
`generateCheckpointAISummary`, `scopeTranscriptForCheckpoint`, and `listCommittedForExplain` all live in the `cli` package and are directly accessible from summary_cmd.go without any import.

Pre-existing ireturn lint violations exist in `agent/capabilities.go` due to nolint comments having been stripped; these show up in `mise lint` output for the whole project but are unrelated to summary TUI work.

`.entire/settings.json` has a `strategy_options.summarize.enabled` flag that was gating the summary command; it was set to true and then the guard was removed entirely so the TUI works unconditionally.

code.finding: ireturn lint fires on `handleGenerate` returning `tea.Model`; fix with `//nolint:ireturn` on the function signature.
IsSummarizeEnabled guard was blocking the entire command; removing it allows the TUI to browse all checkpoints and generate summaries on demand with 'g'.

workflow: Deleting the blocking package (insightsdb) early — before fixing tests — unblocks compilation and gives a clean baseline to work from.
When WIP code references non-existent packages or undefined functions, it's faster to redesign the consuming code than to invent the missing infrastructure.
Unrelated file changes (nolint stripping in capabilities.go) should be reverted before staging to keep commits focused; `git checkout -- capabilities.go` before staging.

friction: `metadataToSessionRow` was referenced in summary_cmd.go but not defined anywhere — took multiple grep rounds to confirm it simply didn't exist yet.
The `facets` import caused a non-obvious build failure; only discovered after trying to compile and seeing the missing directory.
`resolveMemoryLoopDefaultBranch` and `listReachableCheckpointIDs` were called but undefined, requiring the repo-sessions filtering logic to be redesigned from scratch.
Pre-existing ireturn violations in `agent/capabilities.go` appeared in lint output, requiring manual verification that they were not introduced by this work.
Unrelated nolint-stripping changes to `capabilities.go` appeared in the diff and had to be reverted before committing.
open_items: Repo-view branch filtering (originally intended via `listReachableCheckpointIDs`) was simplified to show all checkpoints — branch-scoped filtering in the TUI is deferred.
Facets extraction (scores, tool counts, implementation rationale, tradeoffs, codebase patterns) was entirely removed; if these metrics are wanted later, a new approach not backed by SQLite is needed.
The `--me` flag (owner identity filtering) was removed since checkpoint metadata doesn't include owner info; would require a different identity source to re-add.
Pre-existing ireturn lint issues in `agent/capabilities.go` remain unfixed.
